 Adelaide 36ers Form 
 This looks a close contest on paper, but Adelaide are narrowly favoured to get the job done. New Zealand have lost three of their last four matches, while the 36ers have won five of the last six meetings between the teams. 
 Cotton is the standout player selection after scoring 30+ points in three of his last four matches. The five-time NBL MVP has also reached that mark in four of his last six appearances against the Breakers, making another big scoring performance a strong possibility. 
 The Under 181.5 total points selection is supported by both teams' scoring trends. New Zealand concede the fewest points in the competition at 88.7 per game, while Adelaide rank last in scoring at 89.3. The Breakers are eighth in offensive production, and the 36ers rank fourth defensively, pointing towards a relatively low-scoring encounter.

 New Zealand Breakers Form
 New Zealand have struggled for consistency, losing three of their last four matches despite showing some promising signs at home. The Breakers have won their first two home games of the NBL27 season and their last four at Spark Arena across seasons. 
 Defence has been their biggest strength, conceding a league-low 88.7 points per game. Their opponents are shooting just 44.7% from the field, with New Zealand ranking among the competition's better defensive teams. 
 Sam Mennenga has been a standout performer, averaging 23.1 points and 9.0 rebounds per game. However, the Breakers rank eighth in scoring at 91.2 points per game, and their inconsistent offence has contributed to a 4-5 record. 
 Adelaide 36ers Form
 Adelaide have also experienced an inconsistent start to the season, with four wins from nine matches. Their away record has been more encouraging, winning three of six games on the road. 
 Cotton continues to carry much of the offensive responsibility, averaging a league-leading 27.4 points per game. His recent scoring form has been particularly impressive, with three 30-point performances in his last four outings. 
 The 36ers average just 89.3 points per game, the lowest figure in the competition, but their defence has kept them competitive. Adelaide concede 92.7 points per game, ranking fourth in the NBL, and have won all their games in which they led at half-time.
